name: Hatebreed
label: Victory
lede: A West Haven prep cook's weekend band cut a Victory debut for pocket change, got thrown off Warped Tour, found a home in metal, and put its singer in the host's chair on MTV2's Headbangers Ball.

eras.title: Prep cook by day, breakdowns by weekend
eras.text: Hatebreed came out of the New Haven and West Haven hardcore scene, built around a teenage Jamey Jasta who had been booking shows at The Moon. Half the founders were gone within two years, and the version that cut Satisfaction Is the Death of Desire gave Victory Records its best-selling debut.

years.src: Louder (Metal Hammer): Jamey Jasta, My Life Story · Wikipedia: Jamey Jasta
years.h: Jamey Jasta, 16, starts Hatebreed in his grandfather's car
years.p: Jasta borrowed his grandfather's car to jam with Chris Beattie on bass, Wayne Lozinak and Larry Dwyer Jr. on guitars and Dave Russo on drums. The template was [[Madball|c9e0a0f5-9f53-4247-a52d-a3f29d975e17]], Entombed and [[Earth Crisis|88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8]].
years.xp: Jasta had been going to every kind of show at The Moon in New Haven since he was 12 or 13, and his first band, Dreadnaught (later renamed Jasta 14), opened for [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]]. He told Metal Hammer he worked as a prep cook during the week while Hatebreed practiced and played Thursday to Sunday.

years.h: Under the Knife: Hatebreed's $150 EP
years.p: After a 1995 demo and a split 7" with Neglect, Hatebreed's first EP stalled at Big Wheel Recreation, so the band put it out themselves. Jamey Jasta says it cost $150 of their own money to record.

years.h: Three Hatebreed founders out; Lou "Boulder" Richards in
years.p: Wayne Lozinak, Larry Dwyer Jr. and Dave Russo are gone by the end of 1996. Nick Papantoniou takes the drums for 1996–97 and Lou "Boulder" Richards joins on guitar.

years.h: Hatebreed threatens In/Humanity's Chris Bickel over a zine
years.p: According to Wikipedia, In/Humanity singer Chris Bickel criticized Victory Records in his zine, then was surrounded at a Hatebreed show by band members who threatened him with homophobic slurs.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports that Jamey Jasta later left Bickel a threatening voicemail calling himself a homophobe. In/Humanity played the voicemail at their own shows, and Hatebreed answered with hostile stage banter when they played In/Humanity's hometown of Columbia, South Carolina.

No response from Hatebreed to the account appears in the sources checked.

years.cap: Satisfaction Is the Death of Desire, Victory Records, 1997
years.src: Wikipedia: Satisfaction Is the Death of Desire · Louder (Metal Hammer)
years.h: Satisfaction Is the Death of Desire on Victory
years.p: Produced by [[Steve Evetts|ae091a4c-0a25-4555-8874-5f05768d9d18]], with Matt McIntosh and Lou Richards on guitars and Jamie Pushbutton of [[Death Threat|10bc16b4-567d-4bb0-b455-3ad0db178975]] on drums. Nielsen SoundScan counted 158,000 copies, Victory's best-selling debut.
years.xp:
Signing to Victory got Hatebreed called sellouts: critics called the label the McDonald's of hardcore. Jamey Jasta told Metal Hammer he was heartbroken, and pointed out that [[Strife|5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530]] and [[Integrity|f626335d-d234-408d-a67c-37a3c2c7e98a]] were on Victory too.

The album is what got Hatebreed its Universal deal. Kerrang!, Loudwire and Revolver have all since ranked it among the most important metalcore records ever made.

eras.title: Kicked off Warped, adopted by metal
eras.text: Hatebreed's reputation was chaos: drunk, broke, and banned from the biggest punk tour in America. The metal world took them instead, and a major label bet on a record Jasta built to be as hard as possible.

q: Being thrown off Warped Tour was our push into the metal world.
years.h: Kevin Lyman throws Hatebreed off the Warped Tour
years.p: Hatebreed were kicked off Warped Tour 1998 and banned from coming back. Jamey Jasta blames a young band that was drunk 24 hours a day.
years.xp:
Jasta told Kerrang! the band were drunk and disorderly and gave founder Kevin Lyman a headache, not out of malice. Instead of punk tours, Hatebreed went to Tattoo the Earth in 2000 and made its Ozzfest debut in 2001, the start of four Ozzfest summers.

Nearly twenty years later Hatebreed made peace with Lyman, played his Mayhem Festival in 2010 and 2011, and returned to Warped Tour in 2017.

years.h: Hatebreed vs. Anal Cunt at the New England Metal and Hardcore Festival
years.p: Sound problems moved Hatebreed onto Anal Cunt's stage. According to Anal Cunt's Josh Martin, Jamey Jasta mocked the crowd, then yelled at Seth Putnam, and a melee followed.
years.xp: Wikipedia's account, sourced to Martin, says the crowd was waiting for Anal Cunt and got Hatebreed instead, and Jasta told them Hatebreed sold more records. Putnam and his wife were arrested that night. Hatebreed's side of the story is not in the sources checked.

years.h: Matt Byrne replaces Rigg Ross in the middle of Perseverance
years.p: Hatebreed started recording Perseverance in November 2000. Drummer Rigg Ross left in June 2001, and Matt Byrne finished the sessions. He's still Hatebreed's drummer a quarter century later.

years.src: Wikipedia: Perseverance (Hatebreed album) · Songfacts · Louder (Metal Hammer)
years.h: Perseverance: Hatebreed's Universal debut
years.p: Recorded at Long View Farm in Massachusetts with Matt Hyde, Perseverance debuts at No. 50 on the Billboard 200 and passes 250,000 units by 2022, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Jamey Jasta told Metal Hammer the band made the hardest record it could, to answer the sellout talk. He wrote I Will Be Heard on an acoustic guitar his father gave him, and told Songfacts he knew it would change Hatebreed's career. Lou Richards didn't approve of the song; Jasta went with his gut.

yt: Hatebreed: I Will Be Heard (official video)
years.h: MTV bans Hatebreed's I Will Be Heard video
years.p: The video was directed by Marc Webb, later of The Amazing Spider-Man, and MTV wouldn't play it. The song still landed on the soundtrack to the Vin Diesel film xXx.
years.xp: Jamey Jasta told Metal Hammer in 2025 that the band thought it had wasted a lot of money for nothing. His fix, as he tells it: become the host of Headbangers Ball and play the video himself.

eras.title: The singer takes over the metal show
eras.text: By 2003 Hatebreed was one of the biggest-selling heavy bands in America and its singer was on MTV2 every week. The breakdowns went to Hollywood soundtracks and, in 2005, to the Grammys.

years.h: Jamey Jasta becomes host of MTV2's Headbangers Ball
years.p: Jasta beat Killswitch Engage's Howard Jones for the job and hosted from 2003 to 2007, using the airtime for [[Terror|697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c]], [[Napalm Death|ce7bba8b-026b-4aa6-bddb-f98ed6d595e4]], [[Madball|c9e0a0f5-9f53-4247-a52d-a3f29d975e17]] and the Hatebreed video MTV had banned.

years.h: The Rise of Brutality debuts at No. 30
years.p: Hatebreed's third album sells 32,515 copies in its first week, per Wikipedia. Hatebreed songs turn up in Freddy vs. Jason and Saw around the same time.

years.h: Hatebreed's Live for This is up for a Grammy
years.p: Nominated in December 2004 for Best Metal Performance at the 47th Grammy Awards, Live for This loses to [[Motörhead|57961a97-3796-4bf7-9f02-a985a8979ae9]].

eras.title: Roadrunner, a funeral, a founder back
eras.text: Hatebreed moved to Roadrunner and kept charting, while its singer's side projects ran on alcohol. In 2006 the guitarist from its first two albums died, and by 2009 Jasta was sober and a founder was back in the band.

years.h: Supremacy: Hatebreed's Roadrunner debut
years.p: Hatebreed's fourth album debuts at No. 31 on the Billboard 200 with 27,000 first-week units, then headlines the Monsters of Mayhem tour with [[Napalm Death|ce7bba8b-026b-4aa6-bddb-f98ed6d595e4]] and Exodus.

years.h: Frank Novinec, ex-[[Integrity|f626335d-d234-408d-a67c-37a3c2c7e98a]] and Ringworm, joins Hatebreed
years.p: Frank Novinec had joined Integrity after Systems Overload and played in Cleveland's Ringworm and [[Terror|697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c]]. He debuts on Supremacy and outlasts every other Hatebreed guitarist since.

years.h: Former Hatebreed guitarist Lou "Boulder" Richards dies at 35
years.p: Lou Richards, who played on Satisfaction Is the Death of Desire and Perseverance and left Hatebreed in 2002, died by suicide, according to Wikipedia.
years.xp: Richards was in Hatebreed from 1996 to 2002. Jamey Jasta has credited him with helping craft the band's metalcore sound, and noted to Songfacts that Richards died a month before turning 36.

years.h: Jamey Jasta quits drinking
years.p: Jasta told Metal Hammer he stopped drinking in 2008, after too many forgotten nights, rather than waste the chances he'd been given. In April 2008 Hatebreed signed with Koch Records.
years.xp:
His side projects had been party bands. Kingdom of Sorrow, his sludge band with Crowbar's Kirk Windstein, started on a 2005 UK tour with Crowbar and, by Jasta's account, was recorded wasted. Icepick, running since 1996, put out Violent Epiphany in 2006.

Jasta also remembers one run with Crowbar and Kingdom of Sorrow for wrecked hotel rooms, a smashed bus window and a bus driver who got hit.

years.h: Sean Martin leaves Hatebreed; founder Wayne Lozinak returns
years.p: Sean Martin exits to work on studio projects, and Wayne Lozinak, gone since 1996, comes back on guitar.

years.h: Hatebreed, after a covers album and a No. 1 DVD
years.p: The self-titled album debuts at No. 37. In May came For the Lions, covers of [[Metallica|65f4f0c5-ef9e-490c-aee3-909e7ae6b2ab]], [[D.R.I.|95f6e954-8bed-4f8e-a53e-d155bb6f7ace]], Crowbar and [[Cro-Mags|9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70]]; in September the Live Dominance DVD hit No. 1 on Billboard's DVD chart.

eras.title: A fan's ashes on the stage
eras.text: Twenty years in, Hatebreed hit its chart peak with a steady line-up of Jasta, Beattie, Byrne, Novinec and Lozinak. Jasta built a second career as a podcaster and producer, and the band's past kept surfacing in odd places, from a UFC octagon to a murder trial.

years.h: The Divinity of Purpose: Hatebreed's highest chart peak
years.p: Hatebreed's sixth album of originals reaches No. 20 on the Billboard 200 and No. 1 on the US Hard Rock chart. The cover is by Eliran Kantor.

years.h: UFC makes Chris Camozzi tape over his Hatebreed logos
years.p: Fighter Chris Camozzi, a longtime Hatebreed sponsor, said the UFC required him to cover the band's logos on his shirt and banner with black tape at UFC 158 in Montreal.

years.h: The Concrete Confessional debuts at No. 25
years.p: Hatebreed's seventh album charts high in Belgium, Austria and Switzerland too, and the band tours it around the world through 2017.

years.h: Hatebreed scatter fan Dennis Guyot's ashes on stage in Cleveland
years.p: Granting a dead fan's wish, Hatebreed spread Dennis Guyot's ashes on stage at a Cleveland show, and later wrote As Diehard as They Come in his honor.

eras.title: Thirty years, one lawsuit
eras.text: Hatebreed hit thirty with sold-out anniversary tours and a new album on the way. It also fired its last founder besides Jasta, and the fight went to court in New Haven.

years.h: Weight of the False Self, delayed by COVID
years.p: Hatebreed's eighth album was due in May 2020 and slipped to November. Blabbermouth's Dom Lawson called it the band's strongest album in over a decade.

years.cap: Hatebreed at Reload Festival, 2024. Wikimedia Commons
years.h: Hatebreed turns 30 with a hometown matinee in Wallingford
years.p: Hatebreed opened its 30th anniversary run at Connecticut's Toyota Oakdale Theatre with 100 Demons and [[Shadows Fall|2e3b75d8-00a8-486a-b4e7-a1f8f65e64c9]], then toured Europe with Crowbar and the US with Carcass.

years.h: Hatebreed fires founding bassist Chris Beattie
years.p: Chris Beattie, in Hatebreed since 1994, was separated from the band. In a 2025 interview he said it was not his decision, and that someone saw a chance to get him out.
years.xp:
Matt Bachand of [[Shadows Fall|2e3b75d8-00a8-486a-b4e7-a1f8f65e64c9]] took over bass on tour. Matt Byrne told Blabbermouth he couldn't say much because lawyers were involved.

In 2025 Beattie sued Jamey Jasta, citing a 2015 merchandise agreement; Hatebreed calls him a disgruntled former member of an at-will band. In late May 2026 a Connecticut judge let claims including breach of contract go forward, Lambgoat reported, with a possible jury trial in spring 2027.

years.h: Wayne Lozinak leaves a European tour with a brain tumor
years.p: Lozinak stepped away from Hatebreed's European dates after a brain tumor diagnosis, had successful surgery in August 2025, and was back by October for the Killswitch Engage UK and Ireland tour.

years.h: Hatebreed announces Fatal Paradox, its first album in six years
years.p: Hatebreed signed with BLKIIBLK Records and set Fatal Paradox for November 6, 2026, with the single Kill Count Increase. The first new song in five years, Make the Demons Obey, came out in July 2025.
